sentences: The decision of the New York Philharmonic to hire Alan Gilbert as its next music director has been the talk of the classical-music world ever since the sudden announcement of his appointment in 2009.
For the most part, the response has been favorable, to say the least.
"Hooray! At last!" wrote Anthony Tommasini, a sober-sided classical-music critic.
translations: 纽约爱乐乐团决定聘请艾伦·吉尔伯特担任其下一任音乐总监，这一消息自2009年他突然被任命的消息宣布以来，一直是古典音乐界谈论的话题。
在很大程度上，至少可以说，反应是积极的。
“好哇！终于等到这一天了！”严肃的古典音乐评论家安东尼·托马西尼写道。

sentences: One of the reasons why the appointment came as such a surprise, however, is that Gilbert is comparatively little known.
Even Tommasini, who had advocated Gilbert's appointment in the Times, calls him "an unpretentious musician with no air of the formidable conductor about him."

As a description of the next music director of an orchestra that has hitherto been led by musicians like Gustav Mahler and Pierre Boulez, that seems likely to have struck at least some Times readers as faint praise.
translations: 然而，这一任命之所以如此出人意料，原因之一是吉尔伯特相对而言不太出名。
即使是曾在《纽约时报》上支持任命吉尔伯特的托马西尼，也称他为“一位谦逊的音乐家，没有那种令人敬畏的指挥家的架子。”
对于一个迄今为止一直由古斯塔夫·马勒和皮埃尔·布列兹等音乐家领导的乐团来说，这样的描述似乎很可能至少让一些《纽约时报》的读者觉得是明褒实贬。

sentences: For my part, I have no idea whether Gilbert is a great conductor or even a good one.
To be sure, he performs an impressive variety of interesting compositions, but it is not necessary for me to visit Avery Fisher Hall, or anywhere else, to hear interesting orchestral music.
All I have to do is to go to my CD shelf, or boot up my computer and download still more recorded music from iTunes.
translations: 就我而言，我不知道吉尔伯特是否是一位伟大的指挥家，甚至不知道他是否是一位优秀的指挥家。
诚然，他指挥了种类繁多、令人印象深刻的有趣作品，但我没有必要去艾弗里·费雪音乐厅或其他任何地方听有趣的管弦乐。
我所要做的就是走到我的CD架前，或者启动我的电脑，从iTunes下载更多的录制音乐。

sentences: Devoted concertgoers who reply that recordings are no substitute for live performance are missing the point.

For the time, attention, and money of the art-loving public, classical instrumentalists must compete not only with opera houses, dance troupes, theater companies, and museums, but also with the recorded performances of the great classical musicians of the 20th century.

These recordings are cheap, available everywhere, and very often in much higher artistic quality than today's live performances; moreover, they can be "consumed" at a time and place of the listener's choosing.
The widespread availability of such recordings has thus brought about a crisis in the institution of the traditional classical concert.
translations: 那些回答说录音无法替代现场演出的忠实音乐会常客们没有抓住要点。
为了争夺热爱艺术的公众的时间、注意力和金钱，古典乐器演奏家不仅必须与歌剧院、舞蹈团、戏剧公司和博物馆竞争，还必须与20世纪伟大的古典音乐家的录音表演竞争。
这些录音价格低廉，随处可得，而且其艺术质量往往远高于当今的现场演出；此外，它们可以在听众选择的时间和地点被“消费”。
这类录音的广泛普及因此给传统古典音乐会的体制带来了危机。

sentences: One possible response is for classical performers to program attractive new music that is not yet available on record.

Gilbert's own interest in new music has been widely noted: Alex Ross, a classical-music critic, has described him as a man who is capable of turning the Philharmonic into "a markedly different, more vibrant organization."
But what will be the nature of that difference?
Merely expanding the orchestra's repertoire will not be enough.
If Gilbert and the Philharmonic are to succeed, they must first change the relationship between America's oldest orchestra and the new audience it hopes to attract.
translations: 一个可能的回应是，古典音乐演奏者可以安排演奏那些尚未有录音的、有吸引力的新音乐。
吉尔伯特本人对新音乐的兴趣已被广泛关注：古典音乐评论家亚历克斯·罗斯将他描述为一个能够把爱乐乐团变成“一个明显不同、更有活力的组织”的人。
但是，这种不同的本质是什么呢？
仅仅扩大乐团的曲目是不够的。
如果吉尔伯特和爱乐乐团想要成功，他们必须首先改变美国最古老的乐团与其希望吸引的新观众之间的关系。
